reasoning: Georgia’s recent statewide Senate polling in the last 45 days shows Democrat Jon Ossoff ahead by margins ranging from about D+4 to D+13, with the most cited fresh AARP/Fabrizio-Impact poll at D+9. I found no qualifying Georgia presidential general-election poll in the provided results, so the current race signal is based on the Senate contest; Georgia’s statewide Cook PVI is R+1.2.

sources.name: AARP
sources.details: AARP poll of 1,060 likely Georgia voters found Jon Ossoff leading Mike Collins 52% to 43%, a D+9 margin.

sources.name: The Hill
sources.details: The Hill reported the same AARP/Fabrizio Ward and Impact Research survey showing Ossoff ahead by 9 points.

sources.name: Scripps News
sources.details: Scripps News reported the AARP poll finding Ossoff leading Collins 52-43 among likely voters statewide.

sources.name: Newsweek
sources.details: Newsweek summarized a Wick survey of 1,175 likely voters showing Ossoff over Collins 46.7% to 42.9%, a D+3.8 margin.

sources.name: USA Today
sources.details: USA Today cited a Fox News poll showing Ossoff at 56% and Collins at 43%, a D+13 margin.

sources.name: Pollsmax
sources.details: RealClear-style polling aggregate was not available in the results, but Pollsmax listed a Georgia Senate polling average of Ossoff 49.5% to 42.8%, a D+6.7 average.
